soap.subjective: Female patient with 5-day illness beginning as URI (sore throat, rhinorrhea) progressing to productive cough with yellow-green sputum, fever to 102.4°F, and pleuritic chest pain. Mild exertional dyspnea. Sick contact with coworker who had pneumonia. Vaccinations: influenza current, no pneumococcal vaccine. Penicillin allergy: rash.
soap.objective: Temperature 38.8°C. Heart rate 104. Respiratory rate 20. Blood pressure 118/76. O2 saturation 94% on room air. Auscultation: crackles and decreased breath sounds right lower lobe. CXR: right lower lobe infiltrate. WBC 14,200 with left shift. CURB-65 score 1.

assessment.summary: Community-acquired pneumonia, right lower lobe, mild severity (CURB-65 1). Penicillin allergy precludes beta-lactam therapy. Outpatient treatment appropriate.

plan.instructions: Monitor O2 saturation at home. Return to ED if SpO2 <92% or clinical deterioration. Adequate hydration and rest. Complete full antibiotic course.
plan.follow_up: 5-day recheck. Follow-up CXR in 6 weeks to confirm resolution
